data.central_conflict: The central conflict is both external and internal: externally, the team must overcome technical and environmental obstacles to restore communication when all other infrastructure has failed; internally, they must recognize that their work transcends technical problem-solving and becomes a vital human service. The conflict resolves when they successfully broadcast and understand their new role as community lifeline.
data.logline: When a catastrophic storm cuts off all communication, a team of community radio operators must restore their broadcast to coordinate emergency relief and keep their isolated town connected.
data.narrative_arc: The screenplay follows a classic crisis-response-resolution structure. It opens with immediate catastrophe (storm, infrastructure failure) that forces the protagonists into action. The rising action involves technical problem-solving and the discovery of the broadcast's critical importance to the community. The climax occurs when the first emergency signal is received, validating their efforts. The resolution shows the team operating at full capacity, having transformed from technicians into community anchors. The arc emphasizes that the real story is not about fixing equipment but about restoring human connection and discovering purpose through service.
data.protagonist_journey: The collective protagonist (the four-person team) transforms from isolated technicians focused on equipment repair into purposeful community servants. Individually, each character discovers their role in something larger than themselves. Aria moves from doubt ('Give me ten minutes and one miracle') to confidence as the broadcast succeeds. Noah shifts from cynicism ('I miss boring jobs') to engagement with meaningful work. June evolves from task-focused coordinator to compassionate community voice. Kell transforms from logistics handler to someone who understands the human impact of their work. Together, they journey from crisis response to sustained community commitment.
data.setting_overview: The story takes place in a small town called Red Creek during and immediately after a catastrophic storm that has destroyed cell towers, closed roads, and forced residents to shelter in the high school gym. The primary locations are the community radio studio (the operational hub), the water tower catwalk (where the antenna is installed), and the high school gym shelter (where residents gather and emergency coordination occurs). The time period is contemporary, spanning from late night through the following morning. The world is one where community infrastructure is fragile and interdependent, and where a small radio station can become essential when modern technology fails.
data.synopsis: During a devastating storm that has destroyed cell towers and closed roads, Aria, Noah, June, and Kell work frantically to restore their community radio station to broadcast critical emergency information. With the town's infrastructure failing and residents sheltering in the high school gym, the team races to repair equipment and establish a signal from a water tower relay. As they successfully bring the station back online, they begin broadcasting vital updates about road conditions, shelter supplies, and missing persons, discovering that their small radio station has become the lifeline connecting their fractured community. By morning, with power restored and the broadcast steady, the team realizes their work has transformed them from technicians into essential community anchors, proving that human connection and communication matter most when everything else fails.

themes.description: The screenplay emphasizes how individuals must work together and rely on each other during crisis. The radio station becomes the connective tissue that holds the fractured community together, showing that survival depends on collective effort and shared information.
